finding: Click depth across the entire crawlable site tops out at depth 3 (349 comparison pages), with ZERO unreachable pages and ZERO true orphans (matching growth:google-war's own trueSoftwareOrphans=0 result). This is a genuinely shallow site architecture -- click depth is not a plausible explanation for the indexation gap at the sitewide level, and the indexed-vs-nonindexed comparator (indexed-vs-nonindexed-comparator.json) confirms depth does not separate indexed from not-indexed comparison pages specifically.
nearOrphanNote: 331 comparison pages (24.6% of all 1348) and 9 software pages are flagged 'nearOrphan' (few relevant inbound links, not zero). This is worth tracking but, per the comparator finding, near-orphan status does not correlate with non-indexation any more than the rest of the population -- so this alone should not be treated as the fix for those specific 331 pages without further evidence.
conclusionForPart8: Do not prioritize a click-depth-reduction or internal-linking initiative based on this data. The site's architecture is already shallow; the bottleneck for indexation (where it exists) lies elsewhere per the comparator's own findings.
